To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The isospin-tracing method is a powerful probe of the nonequilibrium in the early stage of heavy-ion collisions; 2) The isospinequilibrium is reached at a much lower centrality than previously thought; 3) The in-medium n-n cross section plays an important role in the stopping and mixing processes in the early stage; and 4) The isospinetracing method is a useful tool to constrain the in-medium n-n interaction.
the global isospin equilibrium is not reached in central collisions of Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr at 400A MeVe, and that the isospin mixing is strongly affected by the in-medium (n,n) cross section.
the degree of mixing between projectile and spectator nucleons is found to be much smaller than that between projectile and target.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of heavy-ion reactions at intermediate and relativistic energies.
the study of nuclear matter under extreme conditions of energy density and temperature, as they exist in the early stage of heavy-ion collisions at relativistic energies.
the physics of nuclear matter under extreme conditions of temperature and/or density.

the isospin mixing is a sensitive and useful tool to probe the degree of nonequilibrium reached in heavy-ion collisions.

we have found evidence of nonequilibrium, and we have quantified it.
the present data are in a good agreement with the predictions of the transport model if the in-medium (n,n) cross section is taken as 2.0 times larger than the free one.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to measure the stopping and mixing properties of heavy-ion collisions in a quantitative and reliable manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isospin mixing is not as efficient as previously thought, even in the most peripheral reactions.
isospin tracing provides a new and powerful probe to investigate nonequilibrium in heavy-ion collisions.
